The union has called for calculating ordinary wages based on 176 monthly work hours and raising wages by 7.85 percent. However, bus companies and the Seoul city government have rejected the demand, saying the proposed calculation would effectively result in a wage increase of approximately 16 percent. The union is threatening to stage a general strike, starting with the first buses at 4 a.m. on Wednesday if no agreement is reached by 9 p.m. Tuesday. snippet: NAGOYA — The national shooting team competing at the Asian Games arrived in the main host city of Nagoya on Tuesday, carrying high hopes for a handful of gold medals. Led by head coach Chang Kap-seok, 30 Korean shooters landed in the central Japanese city five days before the start of their competition. The opening ceremony for the Asian Games is Saturday, and the first shooting medals will be awarded Sunday in the women's 10-meter air rifle individual and team events. Ban Hyo-jin, the 2024 Olympic gold medalist and the 2025 world champion in the 10m individual event, is considered a strong gold medal contender this time. Ban's gold at the 2024 Olympics in Paris was one of six medals by Korea, the most shooting medals the country has won at an Olympics. title: Amid France’s political 'fragmentation', 'a case needs to be made for participatory democracy’
snippet: Carys Garland is pleased to welcome Dr. Andrew Smith, Historian of Modern France and Lecturer in Liberal Arts at Queen Mary University of London. He argues that Marine Le Pen and the National Rally’s commanding position in early presidential polling should not be regarded as an inevitable far-right victory. They are benefiting from familiarity, unity and laser-focused messaging. More fundamentally, however, Smith sees the polling as a reflection of a French electorate shaped by anger, anxiety, economic insecurity and political fatigue.
